text:
alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak I'm seeing a p99 regression on 8k-seq inference jobs, ~+70ms on staging. Reproable.

rachel: Oof. Which change specifically? The selector policy or the batching defaults?

alex: Selector rule change: prefer cuBLAS path when tokens_per_batch > 4096 (was fused-attn for many cases). Also we bumped max_wait_ms to 12 in scheduler config. Paste of latest perf snapshot from perf-bot: 
```
perf_snapshot_id: 177123
kv_hit_rate: 0.92
avg_microbatch_size: 2.1
median_latency_ms: 48
p95_latency_ms: 121
p99_latency_ms: 240
throughput_tokens_per_s: 43k
scheduler: max_batch_tokens=2048, max_wait_ms=12
selector: prefer_cublas_threshold=4096
```

sam: Two quick hypotheses: 1) kernel selection is flipping to a higher-setup-cost path for the typical microbatch shape (many small microbatches), 2) raising max_wait_ms increased queue tail variance so p99 goes up even if median ok.

rachel: Our SLO for interactive chat endpoints is p95 < 150ms and p99 < 250ms. Right now p99 ~240 is borderline but after change it's creeping up on some routes. Need a plan.

alex: Experiment notes: I tried reducing max_wait_ms 12 -> 6; p99 dropped ~30ms but tokens/s dropped ~9%. So it's a SLO vs throughput tradeoff. Lower wait reduces queuing tail but less batching.

sam: Can you share microbatch distribution? If the median microbatch size is tiny we won't amortize kernel launch; kernel selector thresholds should consider microbatch_count and tokens_per_batch separately.

alex: Perf traces show microbatch_count distribution: median=1, p90=3, p99=6. So most requests are singleton microbatches. Kernel change to prefer cuBLAS for big token batches ended up selecting cuBLAS for a few larger aggregated batches but increased variance for small ones.

rachel: Also saw KV-cache behavior correlated: cold-cache spikes line up with the tail samples. Did we change kv-ttl?

alex: Yes — we reduced kv-ttl from 30m -> 10m to fight memory pressure late last week. That raised cold-start rate, so more prefix recomputation and higher tail latencies.

sam: Actionable matrix: sweep across {max_batch_tokens: [1024,2048,4096], max_wait_ms: [4,8,12], kv_ttl: [10m,30m,60m]} and add kernel-selector variations that take microbatch_count into account (e.g., prefer_quant_kernel if microbatch_count >=2; prefer_fused if microbatch_count >=8). Measure median/p95/p99 and tokens/s.

rachel: Add canary route for interactive tier with aggressive low-latency settings (max_wait_ms=3, max_batch_tokens=1024) so we can validate user-facing SLOs without changing default throughput tier.

alex: Quick config snippets I'm going to try: 
```yaml
scheduler:
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  max_wait_ms: 6
kernel_selector:
  rules:
    - if microbatch_count >= 8 -> fused_attn
    - if tokens_per_batch > 4096 and microbatch_count < 8 -> cublas
    - if quantized && microbatch_count >= 2 -> quant_kernel
kv_cache:
  ttl_minutes: 30
```

sam: Good. Also instrument microbatch latency breakdown: kernel_setup_ms vs compute_ms vs kv_fetch_ms vs enqueue_wait_ms; we need the decomposition for the p99 tail.

perf-bot: queued sweep job id=sweep-177123-a (params matrix above). ETA ~2h. Will post aggregated CSV and 95/99 deltas.

rachel: Thanks. One more: tag each sweep with route and traffic profile (interactive vs batch) and include cold-start fraction. We'll need to present tradeoffs to PM/infra.

alex: will do. If kv-ttl revert alone drops p99 by >20ms we can revert that quickly while we iterate on selector heuristics.

sam: If anyone wants to jump on the sweep analysis tomorrow, ping me. Could also try a short A/B: keep current selector but force max_wait_ms=4 for 5% of traffic.

rachel: 👍 sounds like a plan. Keep logs minimal in the thread — link traces instead.

alex: linking perf snapshot: https://perf.internal/runs/177123 and trace examples. Will update when sweep finishes.
